summary: IDS feed s116_double is degraded: 3.80 Gbps microbursts overload the 1 Gbps IDS port (380% capacity, 2 intervals) causing 3.5% TCP packet loss (54 of 1552 packets with sequence gaps). IDS requires full payload and bidirectional flows; gaps break stream reassembly and cause missed detections.

findings.root_cause: Microburst-driven buffer drops: TCP sequence analysis shows 3.5% missing data (54/1552 packets) correlated with 3.80 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port. Feed is noted as sliced, indicating broker is already trying to reduce load but still exceeding port/buffer capacity and dropping packets.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams, misses payload for signature matching, creates false negatives and incomplete alerts; violates needs_full_payload requirement.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple IDS ports/cluster members via packet-broker load balancing to keep per-port rate below 80% of 1 Gbps and eliminate burst drops while preserving full payload

findings.root_cause: Peak 3.80 Gbps in 1 ms burst exceeds IDS 1 Gbps port capacity by 380% (threshold 0.8), with 2 overloaded intervals detected.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port saturated, will indiscriminately drop packets, miss attacks, and risk bypass/fail-open under load; detection coverage severely reduced.

recommended_fix.why: Spread load across 4x1G IDS ports or load-balanced group, or add filtering to cap per-tool throughput below port speed and prevent overload drops
